text:
ana: Quick FYI — I found a set of KMS-wrapped ciphertext blobs in the backup bucket that reference an old wrap key version. No plaintext observed in backups, but we should treat this as a credential exposure risk until we confirm the KEK is fine.
kevin: Can you paste the path and an example blob name?
samir: tagging what to look for: any ciphertext that has the old key version in metadata e.g. keyVersion: 1 or name: projects/.../cryptoKeys/wrap-key/cryptoKeyVersions/1
ana: (typo) sorry, ana: path is gs://redwood-backups/secrets/2026-03-20/wrapped-*.enc — example: wrapped-db-creds-20260320.enc. obj metadata includes: wrapKey: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/kek/cryptoKeys/wrap-key/cryptoKeyVersions/1
jordan: Important question — do we know if that wrap-key version (v1) is still enabled/usable? If it’s been disabled, risk is lower.
ana: (ana) I checked: v1 is still ENABLED and has an IAM binding that includes a few old CI service accounts we deprecated last year.
kevin: OK so attack surface exists if someone got the ciphertext + access to that service account. Let's assume we need an immediate mitigations plan: 1) remove service account entitlements to use the KEK, 2) create a new key version and rewrap ciphertexts, 3) rotate any vault transit keys that were wrapped with it, 4) audit logs for any decrypt operations in the last 90 days.
samir: I can run the IAM prune for the KEK. Proposed command to list bindings: 
```
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy wrap-key --keyring=kek --location=global --project=redwood
```
Then remove the old principals and reapply minimal roles.
jordan: For rewrap, we need a script to iterate backups, call KMS rewrap for each ciphertext into the new key version, and write back. Example rewrap command (gcloud gRPC wrapper):
```
gcloud kms keys versions create --key=wrap-key --keyring=kek --location=global --project=redwood
# use kms rewrap API (pseudo): rewrap --source-key-version=1 --target-key=wrap-key --input-file=blob --output-file=blob.rewrapped
```
nana: (ana) Also must update Vault transit configs: some secrets were double-encrypted (vault transit then KMS-wrapped). We should run a small test to ensure Vault can still unwrap after rewrap or run vault rewrap endpoint.
kevin: Can we get a short maintenance window? I think rewrapping backups is low risk but we should do it with a controlled window and monitoring. Propose a 90-minute window tomorrow 03:00 UTC.
samir: I’ll start IAM pruning at T+0 (first 10m), then create new key version and disable v1 binding. Jordan can run a staged rewrap over a copy of the bucket for validation (env: staging). If tests pass, promote to production.
jordan: I’ll prepare the rewrap job and a dry-run that writes to gs://redwood-backups/rewrapped-check/ — will include integrity checks (SHA256) and metadata update.
nana: For audit, I’ll query Cloud Audit Logs for KMS CryptoKeyDecrypt/CryptoKeyVersions usage:
```
resource.type=\"kms_crypto_key\" protoPayload.methodName=\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\"
```
and search last 365d for the KEK name. If we see unexpected principals, escalate.
pagerbot: Assigned: @samir -> prune KEK IAM, @jordan -> rewrap job + dry-run, @ana -> audit log sweep + post-check, @kevin -> schedule the window and notify infra.
kevin: I scheduled the window 2026-03-21 03:00-04:30 UTC in the infra calendar and added the rollback playbook to the event.
samir: Done with IAM prune draft — will remove deprecated CI service accounts from roles: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter. Pushing change in 5m to infra-iam PR for review.
jordan: Dry-run finished on the sample 50 files, rewrapped, verifications passed. Will start prod rewrap at T+20 after IAM prune completes.
nana: Audit sweep found no decrypts from unknown IPs in last 180d. Two decrypts from a rotated runner account in Jan — I flagged those to eng-sre.
kevin: Good. After rewrap, we should rotate Vault transit key (if used) and invalidate any cached leases that referenced old ciphertext. Plan a quick restart of vault-cluster pods as final step.
samir: IAM PR merged, old principals removed, v1 still exists but with no bindings. Created new key version v3 and set it as primary.
jordan: Prod rewrap started. Copying rewrapped files to gs://redwood-backups/2026-03-20-rewrapped/ and then swapping pointer file once checksum passes.
nana: Post-action: after swap, I’ll run a handful of integration tests from staging apps to ensure they can unwrap and Vault can decrypt as expected.
kevin: Thanks everyone. Can we close this thread after post-checks complete? Add notes to the incident tracker: PRIV-2026-03-KMS-WRAP-CHK. :thumbsup:
nana: will update the tracker and add the PR links and checksums. Closing after one successful run.
